subject: Why Paul said fruit, not fruits
preview: Nine words, one fruit, and it was never meant to be a checklist.
linkText: What Is the Fruit of the Spirit? All 9 Explained

blocks.text: You can probably recite the list from memory.
Love. Joy. Peace. Patience. Kindness. Goodness. Faithfulness. Gentleness. Self control.
Maybe you learned it as a kid, one word per finger.
And then you lose your temper in traffic five minutes later.
Or you pray for more patience and lose it anyway by lunch.
Or you read Galatians 5 and feel guilty on eight out of nine.
If that is you, you are not failing at Christianity.
You are human, and fruit takes time.
Here is a small detail that changes everything.
Paul did not write fruits. He wrote fruit. Singular.
"But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance: against such there is no law."
One fruit with nine parts. It grows together, or it does not grow at all.
The fruit of the Spirit is not a checklist you climb. It is what grows in you when you stay close to Jesus.
A branch does not grunt out apples by trying harder.
It stays attached to the vine, and the vine does the rest.
"I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing."
That does not make growth easy. It means the source is different.
Longsuffering only grows around people who are hard to love.
Temperance stands guard over all the others.
And slow growth is still growth.
He is not in a hurry with you.
In the full guide I walk through all nine, one at a time, straight from Galatians 5, with six simple ways to stay planted where the fruit can grow.
